intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the spectacular Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasting apps to maximize your chances of seeing the lights dance across the sky in vivid greens and purples.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask bar, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The steaming turquoise lagoon surrounded by black lava fields is a surreal and deeply relaxing experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential Northern Lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a scenic rural setting. A perfect off-the-beaten-path alternative with a truly local feel.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the stunning Sólheimajökull glacier with a certified guide. Trek across a dramatic icescape of crevasses, ice caves, and towering seracs while learning about Iceland's volcanic geology and climate change. One of the most thrilling and photogenic adventures available in Iceland.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and rich Viking heritage. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at iconic spots. Visit the Hallgrímskirkja church, the old harbour, and colorful street art murals that define Reykjavik's creative identity.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus or public bus (Route 55) to Reykjavik. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a short orientation walk along the nearby shoreline to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head into central Reykjavik (short bus or walk depending on hotel proximity). Visit Hallgrimskirkja Church for free exterior views and climb the tower for panoramic city views (small fee ~1,500 ISK). Stroll Laugavegur Street. After dark, check the Aurora forecast app and step outside the hotel to scan the sky for your first potential Northern Lights sighting from the dark beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport arrivals hall
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at the airport or a nearby petrol station deli (Orkan/N1) - hot dogs or sandwiches ~700-1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur - Iceland's famous hot dog stand in Reykjavik, iconic and extremely budget-friendly (~500 ISK per hot dog). Grab two and enjoy near the harbor.

day_by_day.notes: Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for Northern Lights forecasts. January darkness begins around 16:00, giving long viewing windows. Exchange some currency or ensure your card works - most places accept Visa/Mastercard. Temperatures likely -2°C to 4°C, dress in warm layers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportid) open on weekends - browse secondhand goods and local snacks cheaply. If not a weekend, explore the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (free entry) or walk along Saebraut coastal path. Stop at Grotta Lighthouse at the tip of the Seltjarnarnes peninsula - free access and a known Northern Lights viewing spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Solfar) along the waterfront - free iconic photo stop. Walk to Harpa Concert Hall and admire the stunning glass facade (free to enter lobby). Explore the Old Harbour area and browse fish markets. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (871+/-2) to learn about Viking-age Reykjavik (~2,200 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunt from the Grotta Lighthouse or Grótta beach area near the hotel - one of Reykjavik's best dark sky spots. Bring a thermos of hot tea. If aurora activity is low (KP index below 3), enjoy the clear coastal night sky. Check forecast before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Make your own at the hotel if kitchen facilities available, or visit a local bakery like Braud & Co for a fresh pastry and coffee (~800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch at Hlolla Bátar soup and sandwich shop (~1,500-2,000 ISK) or a grocery store like Bonus (yellow pig sign) for self-catered sandwiches
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal from Bonus supermarket ingredients (pasta, sauce, bread) - budget approximately 1,500-2,000 ISK for groceries for two meals

day_by_day.notes: Bonus supermarket is Iceland's cheapest grocery chain - stock up on snacks, water, and easy meal ingredients to save significantly on food costs throughout the trip. January KP index of 3+ gives good Northern Lights chances from dark coastal areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Golden Circle (rent a car for the day or join a budget group tour ~8,000-12,000 ISK). First stop: Thingvellir National Park - walk the Almannagjá canyon where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Free entry to the park. Walk the rift valley trail for stunning geology views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Geysir geothermal area - watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes (free entry to the geothermal field). Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall - one of Iceland's most powerful and beautiful waterfalls, free to visit. Walk to the upper and lower viewpoints for dramatic winter views, possibly with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik. On the drive back through Thingvellir, pull over at a dark area away from light pollution for Northern Lights viewing. The open landscape provides 360-degree sky views. Return to hotel and warm up with hot drinks.

meals.breakfast: Pack a self-made breakfast from Bonus groceries before departing early
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the supermarket to eat at Geysir or Gullfoss - avoid the expensive tourist cafes at these sites
meals.dinner: Cozy budget dinner at Reykjavik's Aktu Taktu fast food restaurant (~1,500-2,000 ISK for burger and fries) or cook at hotel

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300km round trip. Renting a car with 3-4 fellow travelers splits costs significantly. Book car rental in advance - small economy cars start around 8,000-12,000 ISK/day in January. Roads may be icy - check road conditions at road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula - drive or take a bus toward the Blue Lagoon area. Walk the free Reykjanes lava fields and visit the Bridge Between Continents (free) - a small footbridge symbolically spanning the two tectonic plates. Explore the dramatic volcanic landscape around Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon area - while the Blue Lagoon itself is expensive (~12,000-20,000 ISK), the nearby Grindavik town has the budget-friendly Sky Lagoon alternative or simply enjoy the free exterior views of the steaming geothermal landscape. Consider visiting the Svartsengi geothermal power plant viewpoint (free). Walk around the lava fields surrounding the area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel. This evening, take a dedicated Northern Lights tour from your hotel area or join a free self-guided hunt along the dark beachfront. The Reykjanes Peninsula's low light pollution makes it excellent for aurora viewing. Set an alarm for midnight for a second check if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or self-made from groceries
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bonus supermarket eaten in the car or at a scenic viewpoint
meals.dinner: Try a local Grindavik fish and chips shop or return to Reykjavik for Saegreifinn (Sea Baron) lobster soup - a beloved budget seafood spot (~2,500 ISK for a bowl)

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula experienced volcanic activity in recent years - check current safety advisories at safetravel.is before visiting. The area is geologically fascinating but conditions can change. Sky Lagoon entry is ~9,000-11,000 ISK if you choose to splurge on one hot spring experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjavik's geothermal swimming pools - the ultimate local experience. Head to Laugardalslaug (largest public pool in Iceland, ~1,000 ISK entry) or the closer Sundhöllin pool. Soak in the outdoor hot pots (naturally heated to 38-44°C), steam rooms, and saunas. This is how locals relax and it's incredibly affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Laugardalur park area around the pool complex - visit the free outdoor areas, botanical garden, and walking paths. Head to the Reykjavik Zoo and Family Park if interested (small entry fee). Walk or take bus back through the city, stopping at Hallgrimskirkja interior (free) and the nearby Einar Jonsson Sculpture Garden (free outdoor garden).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights forecast check - if KP index is 3 or above and skies are clear, take a bus or taxi to Oskjuhlid Hill (the Perlan building area) for elevated dark sky views over the city. The hill provides good panoramic views away from the brightest city lights. Alternatively, walk to the Seltjarnarnes peninsula tip.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered from Bonus groceries - oatmeal, yogurt, or toast
meals.lunch: Try the Hlemmur Food Hall for budget bites (~1,500-2,500 ISK) - various food stalls with diverse options
meals.dinner: Noodle Station on Laugavegur - excellent budget Asian noodle soup, very popular with locals (~1,800-2,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Iceland's public swimming pools are a cultural institution - bring your own towel and swimsuit to avoid rental fees. Showering before entering the pool is mandatory (no swimsuit required in shower area - this is normal Icelandic custom). Pool entry is one of the best budget experiences in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2-hour drive from Reykjavik - rent a car or join a budget group tour). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park - the glacier volcano immortalized in Jules Verne's Journey to the Center of the Earth. Drive the scenic Route 54 along the peninsula's south coast with dramatic mountain and lava field views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arnarstapi village and the stunning coastal basalt rock formations and sea arch (free). Walk the trail to Hellnar village along the dramatic cliff coastline. Visit Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the rusted shipwreck remnants (free). Explore Vatnshellir lava tube cave if budget allows (~3,500 ISK for guided tour).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls (~15:30-16:00 in January). The drive through the Snæfellsnes Peninsula offers excellent Northern Lights viewing opportunities away from city lights. Pull over at any dark area with clear skies. Return to hotel by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch from supermarket - this is a long day trip with limited budget food options on the peninsula
meals.dinner: Stop at the Freezer Hostel in Rif village for affordable food if timing works, or eat at hotel upon return

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 200km from Reykjavik. January roads can be challenging - check road.is and weather forecasts. The peninsula is less visited in winter, making it excellent for dark skies and Northern Lights. A full-day rental car is recommended for flexibility. Fuel up before leaving Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Sleep in after several active days. Visit the hotel's beachfront for a morning walk as daylight arrives (~10:30 in January). Catch up on journaling, photo editing, or planning. Visit a nearby Bonus supermarket to restock supplies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Museum of Iceland in Reykjavik (~2,000 ISK entry, free on certain days) - excellent overview of Icelandic history and culture. Walk through the museum's Viking artifacts, medieval treasures, and modern history exhibits. Afterward, browse the nearby university area and Tjornin lake (free) - often partially frozen in January with photogenic ice.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights evening - check the aurora forecast carefully. If conditions are favorable (clear skies, KP 3+), take a taxi or drive to Mosfellsbaer or Hafnarfjordur on the outskirts of Reykjavik for darker skies. Bring warm layers, a tripod for photos, and a flask of hot chocolate. Stay out for 1-2 hours scanning the northern horizon.

meals.breakfast: Lazy hotel breakfast or self-catered - treat yourself to fresh pastries from a local bakery
meals.lunch: Cozy lunch at Cafe Babalú on Skólavördustígur - quirky budget-friendly cafe with soups and sandwiches (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from Bonus - cook pasta, soup, or buy ready meals to save budget for upcoming experiences

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for a 13-day trip. Use this time to review your budget spending and adjust plans accordingly. January is statistically one of the best months for Northern Lights in Iceland due to long dark nights (up to 19 hours of darkness). Keep checking the aurora forecast daily.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to South Iceland - rent a car for a multi-day road trip along the South Coast (most cost-effective if shared with other travelers). Drive Route 1 (Ring Road) east from Reykjavik. First major stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall - walk behind the cascading waterfall (free, but potentially icy in January - check safety conditions). Then visit nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden canyon waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall - one of Iceland's most spectacular (free entry). Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views over the South Coast. In winter, the waterfall often has dramatic ice formations. Continue to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vik - dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean here - sneaker waves are deadly.
day_by_day.evening: Check into budget accommodation in Vik or nearby (guesthouses/hostels ~5,000-8,000 ISK per night). Vik is an excellent Northern Lights viewing location. After dinner, walk to the black beach or the hill above town for aurora hunting. The dark skies away from Reykjavik significantly improve viewing chances.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast before departure from hotel
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from Reykjavik Bonus - eat at Seljalandsfoss or Skógafoss
meals.dinner: Sudur-Vík restaurant in Vik for affordable Icelandic fish or lamb soup (~2,500-3,500 ISK) or self-catered if accommodation has kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Book South Coast accommodation in advance - options are limited in small towns. Vik is approximately 180km from Reykjavik (2.5 hours in winter conditions). Fill up on fuel before leaving Reykjavik and again at every opportunity - petrol stations are sparse. Download offline maps as cell service can be patchy.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning at Reynisfjara black beach to catch the limited winter sunrise light (~10:30). Drive east to Skaftafell area within Vatnajökull National Park (free park entry). Hike to Svartifoss waterfall through the park - a stunning 1.5-hour round trip hike through birch forest to a waterfall surrounded by dark basalt columns. Free and spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget glacier hiking tour on Falljökull or Svinafellsjökull glacier (~9,000-12,000 ISK including crampons and guide - mandatory for safety). This is one of Iceland's most unique experiences and relatively affordable compared to other countries. Alternatively, walk to the glacier lagoon viewpoints for free if budget is tight. Visit the Skaftafell visitor center (free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approximately 50km east of Skaftafell). Arrive as darkness falls for a magical experience - the floating blue icebergs are illuminated by moonlight or potentially the Northern Lights reflecting off the water. This is one of Iceland's most photographed Northern Lights locations. Stay for 1-2 hours of aurora hunting.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered from packed supplies at accommodation
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Skaftafell visitor center picnic area
meals.dinner: Simple self-catered dinner at accommodation near Jökulsárlón or the small cafe at the glacier lagoon (limited hours in winter)

day_by_day.notes: Book glacier hiking in advance - tours fill up even in winter. Wear waterproof boots and warm layers. Jökulsárlón is approximately 375km from Reykjavik and 80km east of Skaftafell. Consider staying near the glacier lagoon for the night to maximize aurora viewing time. Diamond Beach (just east of the lagoon) has ice chunks washed ashore on black sand - stunning for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn visit to Diamond Beach (Breiðamerkursandur) - the black sand beach adjacent to Jökulsárlón where transparent ice chunks wash ashore. Magical in winter morning light. Then visit the glacier lagoon itself as daylight improves - watch icebergs calve and float in the milky blue water. Free to visit and walk around the lagoon edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin driving back west along the Ring Road. Stop at Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon (check accessibility - sometimes closed in winter) - a stunning 2km long, 100m deep canyon with a free walking trail. Continue to Kirkjubæjarklaustur (Klaustur) - a small village with a free waterfall walk to Systrafoss and the Kirkjugólf basalt floor formations.
day_by_day.evening: Continue west toward Vik or find accommodation midway. Stop at any dark pull-off along Route 1 for Northern Lights viewing - the South Coast has minimal light pollution. The Myrdalssandur black sand desert area provides excellent open sky views. Check aurora forecast and plan a dedicated viewing stop.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast at Diamond Beach - memorable dining experience
meals.lunch: N1 petrol station lunch in Klaustur - surprisingly decent and budget-friendly (~1,000-1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at accommodation or small guesthouse meal if available (~2,000-3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Jökulsárlón back to Vik is approximately 180km (2.5 hours). Road conditions in January can be challenging - check road.is constantly. The Myrdalssandur area can have severe winds - exercise caution when stopping. Keep fuel tank above half at all times in this remote region.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Þórsmörk (Thorsmork) nature reserve if accessible by 4WD vehicle (check conditions - may require a super jeep in January). Alternatively, hike the Fimmvörðuháls trail starting point near Skógar for winter views. Or visit the Eyjafjallajökull glacier and Solheimajökull glacier tongue (free to walk to the glacier edge - check safety signs).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward Reykjavik along the South Coast. Stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake (~400 ISK entry - one of Iceland's most affordable geological wonders). Walk the rim of the 3,000-year-old crater and down to the vivid blue-green lake. Continue to Hveragerdi hot spring town - walk the free geothermal park in town center with bubbling hot springs and steaming vents.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik and your hotel. Celebrate the South Coast road trip with a slightly nicer dinner than usual. After dinner, take a final evening walk along the beachfront from your hotel - the coastal location offers good Northern Lights viewing if conditions permit. Reflect on the week's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered packed breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Hveragerdi bakery or cafe for fresh bread and soup (~1,200-1,800 ISK) - a charming local stop
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to Reykjavik's Messinn restaurant for pan-fried fish (~3,500-4,500 ISK) or Sægreifinn lobster soup as a South Coast celebration meal

day_by_day.notes: Hveragerdi has a natural hot spring river (Reykjadalur) accessible via a 3km hike where you can bathe in the river for free - this is an incredible budget hot spring experience. The hike takes about 45 minutes each way. Bring a swimsuit and towel. Check trail conditions in January as it can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjadalur hot spring river near Hveragerdi (if not done yesterday) - hike 3km to the geothermal river and soak in natural hot springs for free. This is arguably the best free hot spring experience in Iceland. Alternatively, visit the Laugarvatn Fontana geothermal baths on the Golden Circle route (~4,500 ISK) for a more developed but still affordable hot spring experience with lakeside steam rooms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for a final afternoon of city exploration. Visit the Perlan museum - the rotating glass dome building with a free observation deck offering 360-degree views of Reykjavik and surrounding mountains. The Northern Lights exhibition inside is worth seeing (~2,900 ISK entry) with a simulated aurora experience. Browse Laugavegur for any last-minute souvenirs (avoid tourist shops - try Kolaportid flea market for cheaper finds).
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated Northern Lights hunt. Take a taxi or drive to Akranes (45 minutes north of Reykjavik) or Mosfellsbaer for dark sky viewing. Alternatively, join a last-chance Northern Lights tour (~8,000-10,000 ISK) with guides who know the best local spots and will drive you to clear sky areas. This is worth the splurge on the final night.

meals.breakfast: Special final-days breakfast at a local cafe - try Sandholt Bakery on Laugavegur for exceptional pastries and coffee (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Hlemmur Food Hall for a varied budget lunch (~1,500-2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Icelandic Street Food - affordable traditional Icelandic lamb soup served in a bread bowl (~2,000-2,500 ISK) on Laugavegur

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags tonight for early departure tomorrow. Keep one warm outfit accessible for the morning. If you haven't seen the Northern Lights yet, tonight is your last real chance - prioritize a dedicated aurora hunt regardless of cost. The Vedur app KP forecast is most accurate within 2 hours. Clear skies plus KP 3+ equals good viewing odds.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a leisurely breakfast and a last walk along the beachfront from the hotel. Breathe in the fresh Icelandic sea air and take final photos of the dramatic winter landscape. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange transport to Keflavik Airport (Flybus from BSI terminal or pre-booked airport transfer ~3,000-4,000 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik Airport with ample time (2-3 hours before international departure). Browse duty-free for Icelandic gifts - Icelandic chocolates, Skyr, and local spirits are good value in duty-free. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Northern Lights hunting, hot springs, glaciers, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry memories of Iceland's otherworldly beauty, the dancing green lights of the aurora borealis, and the warmth of geothermal waters against the cold Arctic air.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast at hotel or a nearby bakery - treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal
meals.lunch: Airport food (budget approximately 2,000-3,000 ISK for airport prices) or pack remaining snacks from your Bonus supplies
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips: Total estimated daily budget ~8,000-15,000 ISK (€55-105) per person including accommodation, food, and activities if planned carefully. Biggest savings come from: Bonus supermarket groceries, public swimming pools instead of expensive spas, free natural attractions (waterfalls, beaches, lava fields), and sharing car rental costs. Northern Lights are never guaranteed but January offers 18+ hours of darkness and statistically good aurora activity. Hope you caught the lights!

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the spectacular Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasting apps to maximize your chances of seeing the lights dance across the sky in vivid greens and purples.

experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask bar, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The steaming turquoise lagoon surrounded by black lava fields is a surreal and deeply relaxing experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential Northern Lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a scenic rural setting. A perfect off-the-beaten-path alternative with a truly local feel.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00 (Keflavík International Airport). Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 45–60 min drive). Settle into your beachfront room and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate surroundings of the resort and nearby coastline. Take a leisurely beachfront walk to acclimatize to Iceland's January light and crisp air. Visit a local supermarket (Bónus or Krónan) to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town for a relaxed first dinner. Stroll around to get oriented. Return to the resort early to rest after the flight and prepare for the days ahead. Keep an eye on aurora forecasts – January nights offer long darkness windows.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight meal or airport snack on arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Keflavík Airport (Pylsuvagninn hot dog stand or airport café) – budget-friendly classic Icelandic hot dog (~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the resort – try Icelandic fish soup and lamb stew at a local grill house (~3,500–5,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest and orientation. Download the Veður app (Icelandic Met Office) and Aurora Forecast app for real-time aurora and weather updates throughout the trip. January sunset is around 16:30–17:00, so darkness sets in early.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booked Comfort package recommended, ~12,000–15,000 ISK). Arrive early (9:00–10:00) to beat crowds. Soak in the iconic milky-blue silica-rich geothermal waters, enjoy an in-water silica mud mask, and use the steam caves and sauna facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. After relaxing, drive or take a short trip to Reykjanes Peninsula coastal cliffs and the Bridge Between Continents – a footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Free to visit and a stunning geological highlight.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour – join a small-group guided tour departing from a nearby meeting point. The expert guide will drive the group away from light pollution to optimal viewing locations based on that night's aurora forecast (KP index dependent). Tour typically runs 21:00–00:00.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort or a nearby café – Skyr with granola and fresh juice (~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the Blue Lagoon's LAVA Restaurant or the casual café inside the lagoon complex – soup and sandwich (~3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Early dinner before the Northern Lights tour – try a local bistro with Icelandic lamb burger or fish and chips (~3,000–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon well in advance – January is popular despite being off-peak. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone at the lagoon. For the Northern Lights tour, dress in thermal base layers, mid-layer fleece, and a windproof outer shell. Temperatures can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjavík (approx. 45 min from the resort). Explore the city's iconic landmarks: Hallgrímskirkja Church (take the elevator to the top for panoramic views, ~1,000 ISK), and the striking Harpa Concert Hall by the harbor. Walk along Laugavegur street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) to learn about Viking history and Icelandic culture (~2,000 ISK entry). Afterward, explore the colorful streets of the 101 Reykjavík district, pop into local design shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavík's vibrant but intimate dining scene for dinner. Return to the resort by 22:00 and check aurora forecast for potential late-night viewing from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at resort included or grab pastries at a Reykjavík bakery – Brauð & Co is a beloved local spot (~1,200 ISK)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja – traditional Icelandic rye bread with smoked lamb and herring (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) – famous lobster soup and grilled fish skewers at mid-range prices (~3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Parking in Reykjavík city center is metered. Alternatively, use the Strætó bus app if you prefer public transport. January days are short (~5 hours of light), so plan outdoor sightseeing between 11:00 and 15:30 to maximize daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Golden Circle route – start with Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Walk the Almannagjá canyon rift valley where tectonic plates meet. Explore the historical site of Iceland's first parliament (Alþingi, est. 930 AD). Free entry to the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water up to 30 meters. Walk the surrounding hot spring fields. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall – one of Iceland's most powerful and dramatic waterfalls, especially stunning with winter ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort via the Golden Circle loop (approx. 2-hour drive). Stop for dinner en route. Check aurora forecast for late evening viewing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure (~07:30)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Geysir Center restaurant – hearty lamb soup and bread (~2,800 ISK) or pack a picnic from the resort
meals.dinner: Dinner at a roadside restaurant on the return route – Friðheimar tomato farm restaurant (book ahead) or a guesthouse restaurant (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Rent a car if you haven't already – a 4WD is strongly recommended in January. Roads can be icy; check road conditions at road.is before departure. Wear ice cleats (yaktrax) for walking near Gullfoss in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast and use the resort amenities. Alternatively, take a morning walk along the beachfront to watch the sunrise (around 11:00 in January) over the Atlantic – a dramatic and peaceful experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (~1.5 hours from the resort). Iceland's oldest swimming pool (est. 1891) is a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by geysers and hot springs. More rustic and authentic than the Blue Lagoon. Entry ~3,000 ISK. Soak for 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour (second attempt or alternative evening if first tour was cloudy). The guide will select the best viewing location based on current aurora activity. Alternatively, self-drive to a dark sky location near the resort if aurora forecast is strong (KP ≥ 3).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort – eggs, Skyr, smoked salmon, and fresh bread
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Flúðir village near the Secret Lagoon – local café or packed lunch (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby spot – grilled Arctic char with roasted root vegetables (~4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more authentic local experience. The surrounding mini-geysers and steaming vents are especially atmospheric in the dark of January. Book Secret Lagoon tickets online in advance. Bring a towel and swimsuit.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the South Coast toward Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (~1.5 hours from the resort). In winter, you may be able to walk behind the waterfall (check conditions – it can be icy and closed). The frozen mist and ice formations make it magical in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall – one of Iceland's largest and most impressive waterfalls. Climb the staircase to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast. Then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík – stunning basalt column formations and dramatic sea stacks. Caution: sneaker waves are dangerous; stay back from the waterline.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort (approx. 2 hours). Stop for dinner in a town along the South Coast. Aurora watch from the car or a designated dark spot on the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógafoss Visitor Center café or a packed lunch – lamb sandwich and hot thermos of coffee (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Halldórskaffi in Hvolsvöllur or a South Coast guesthouse restaurant – traditional meat soup and fish of the day (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 250–300 km round trip. January road conditions can be challenging; check road.is every morning. The black sand beach at Reynisfjara is one of the most photographed in Iceland – bring a wide-angle lens if you have one. Sunset creates incredible golden-hour light on the cliffs around 15:30–16:00.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed mid-trip recovery day. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast at the resort, and review photos from the first week. Use the resort's spa or pool facilities if available. Plan the second half of the trip and confirm any remaining bookings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula more deeply – visit Gunnuhver Hot Springs (largest hot spring in Iceland), the Reykjanes Lighthouse (Iceland's oldest), and the Valahnúkamöl cliffs with dramatic basalt rock formations and crashing Atlantic waves. All free and accessible within 30–45 minutes of the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:30) over the Reykjanes Peninsula cliffs is spectacular. Stay for the golden and blue hours, then head back to the resort for a comfortable dinner and aurora watch from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – take your time
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the Reykjanes cliffs – thermos of soup, rye bread with smoked salmon, and Skyr (~prepared from supermarket, ~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant – try the Icelandic lamb rack with root vegetable purée (~4,500–6,000 ISK for a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally balanced – half exploration, half rest. The Reykjanes Peninsula is geologically one of the most active areas in Iceland and was the site of recent volcanic eruptions (2021–2024 Fagradalsfjall eruptions). The landscape is raw and otherworldly. Stay on marked paths near Gunnuhver as the ground can be unstable.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approx. 2.5 hours from the resort). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park and the iconic glacier volcano that inspired Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk the Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach with its mysterious shipwreck remnants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi and the dramatic Hellnar coastal cliffs. Walk the 2.5 km coastal trail between Arnarstapi and Hellnar for breathtaking winter scenery. Visit Vatnshellir lava tube cave (guided tours available, ~3,500 ISK).
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive toward the resort (2.5 hours). This is a long day – consider stopping for dinner in Borgarnes on the way back. Check aurora forecast for late evening viewing on the drive.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the long drive
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Settlement Center in Borgarnes on the way – excellent lamb soup and Viking-era exhibition (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Borgarnes at Settlement Center Restaurant or a local café on the return journey (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day trip from the resort. Start no later than 08:30 to maximize the limited daylight. Road 54 around the peninsula can be icy in January – 4WD essential. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' as it contains glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, and dramatic coastline all in one area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Lava Center in Hvolsvöllur (approx. 1.5 hours from the resort) – a world-class interactive exhibition about Icelandic volcanism, earthquakes, and geothermal energy. Entry ~3,500 ISK. Excellent context for understanding the landscapes you've been exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Þórsmörk Valley (if accessible in January – check conditions). Alternatively, explore the Eyjafjallajökull glacier area and the Fljótshlíð valley farmlands with views of the glacier that famously erupted in 2010. Visit the Eyjafjallajökull Visitor Center at Þorvaldseyri farm (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour (third opportunity if previous tours were clouded out) or self-drive aurora hunt. Return to resort for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café in Hvolsvöllur near the Lava Center (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort or a nearby restaurant – Icelandic fish stew or pan-fried cod with butter sauce (~3,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Þórsmörk is a highland area and may be inaccessible in January without a super-jeep. Confirm road conditions at road.is. The Eyjafjallajökull Visitor Center at Þorvaldseyri is a free and fascinating stop with personal accounts from the 2010 eruption from the farm family who lived through it.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Reykjavík for a deeper cultural day. Visit the Perlan Museum (Wonders of Iceland) – stunning glass dome building with aurora exhibition, ice cave tunnel, and 360° panoramic views of the city (~4,500 ISK). One of the best aurora-related exhibits in Iceland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavík's art scene – visit the Reykjavík Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) featuring Icelandic landscape paintings (~2,000 ISK). Browse the flea market at Kolaportið (open weekends) for local crafts, vintage items, and traditional Icelandic food like hákarl (fermented shark) if you're adventurous.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavík's Saturday night dining and atmosphere. The city has a lively but manageable nightlife scene. Return to the resort by 23:00.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before driving to Reykjavík
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kolaportið flea market – try traditional Icelandic snacks and street food (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Messinn restaurant in Reykjavík – renowned for cast-iron skillet fish of the day, excellent value (~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Perlan Museum's aurora exhibition is an excellent complement to the real aurora experiences on this trip. The indoor ice cave tunnel replicates a Vatnajökull glacier cave. Book Perlan tickets online. Kolaportið flea market is only open on weekends (11:00–17:00).

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Enjoy the beachfront, resort amenities, and a slow breakfast. Pack a daypack for a scenic afternoon excursion. Review and back up all your trip photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Krýsuvík Geothermal Area on the Reykjanes Peninsula (approx. 30 min from the resort) – free and accessible. Walk the boardwalk trails through vivid sulfurous hot springs, mud pots, and steaming fumaroles in a lunar-like landscape. Nearby Lake Kleifarvatn offers dramatic winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Guided Tour (if not yet seen, or for another chance at better conditions) OR a self-guided aurora hunt from a dark coastal spot near the resort. Pack hot drinks in a thermos. If aurora is not active, enjoy a peaceful evening at the resort reflecting on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full leisurely breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café or packed snacks for the Krýsuvík visit
meals.dinner: Special mid-trip dinner at the resort's restaurant or a nearby upscale-casual spot – splurge slightly on Icelandic langoustine or lamb (~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Krýsuvík is one of the most accessible and impressive geothermal areas in Iceland and is completely free. The colors of the mineral deposits – yellows, oranges, and greens – are vivid even in winter. Stay strictly on the boardwalks as the ground around hot springs can be dangerously thin. The area is best visited in the afternoon when any available light illuminates the steam.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north to the Snæfellsnes area or west to the Westfjords border region for a final big-day adventure. Alternatively, revisit a favorite location from earlier in the trip with fresh eyes. Consider a guided glacier walk on Sólheimajökull glacier (approx. 2 hours from the resort, ~15,000 ISK with gear rental) – an unforgettable experience on an Icelandic glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: If doing the glacier walk, the guided tour typically runs 09:00–14:00. Afternoon free to explore the South Coast surroundings or drive back at a relaxed pace. Stop at any viewpoints or locations you want to revisit or photograph again with better conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a farewell dinner. Pack non-essential items and prepare luggage for departure the following day. Final aurora watch from the beachfront – January 26th still offers excellent aurora-watching conditions.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch near Sólheimajökull glacier – packed lunch or visitor center café (~2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort – order something memorable from the menu, share highlights of the trip (~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Sólheimajökull glacier walk requires booking in advance with a certified guide. Crampons and harnesses are provided. Minimum age and fitness requirements apply. The glacier has retreated significantly due to climate change – walking on it is both awe-inspiring and sobering. If the glacier walk doesn't appeal, a scenic drive along Route 1 with stops at viewpoints is equally rewarding.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Wake up for one last sunrise (around 10:30–11:00). Take a final walk along the beachfront of Aegean Bliss Resort. Check out of the resort, ensuring luggage is packed and the room is cleared by check-out time (typically 11:00–12:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Keflavík International Airport (allow at least 1.5–2 hours before flight departure for check-in, security, and any last-minute duty-free shopping). Browse the airport's Icelandic souvenir shops for lopapeysa wool sweaters, lava salt, Skyr products, and Brennivín schnapps as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days in Iceland – Northern Lights, geothermal pools, volcanic landscapes, waterfalls, and the unique magic of Iceland in January.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort – savor it
meals.lunch: Lunch at Keflavík Airport – Icelandic hot dog (pylsur) at the airport kiosk for a classic farewell bite (~500–800 ISK)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at the destination airport

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan the resort check-out accordingly. Keflavík Airport is approximately 45–55 minutes from most Reykjanes Peninsula accommodations. Allow extra time in January for potential icy road conditions. The airport duty-free is well-stocked and competitively priced for Icelandic products – stock up on Skyr, Icelandic salt, and spirits after passport control.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Guided Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the spectacular Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasting apps to maximize your chances of seeing the lights dance across the sky in vivid greens and purples.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, a silica mud mask bar, and a swim-up bar serving Icelandic craft beer. The steaming turquoise lagoon surrounded by black lava fields is a surreal and deeply relaxing experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential Northern Lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic hot spring sits amid bubbling geysers and steaming vents in a scenic rural setting. A perfect off-the-beaten-path alternative with a truly local feel.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the stunning Sólheimajökull glacier with a certified guide. Trek across a dramatic icescape of crevasses, ice caves, and towering seracs while learning about Iceland's volcanic geology and climate change. One of the most thrilling and photogenic adventures available in Iceland.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its culinary scene and rich Viking heritage. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at iconic spots. Visit the Hallgrímskirkja church, the old harbour, and colorful street art murals that define Reykjavik's creative identity.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll along the shoreline to acclimate to the Icelandic winter atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booked premium package): Just 20 minutes from the airport and near the resort, soak in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water silica mud mask treatments, a private changing suite, and a welcome sparkling wine. Ideal way to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Onboard flight meal
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack and Champagne at the resort upon check-in
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — Iceland's premier geothermal dining experience featuring locally sourced seafood and New Nordic cuisine with views over the lagoon

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon is only 20 minutes from Keflavík Airport — perfect for a Day 1 stop before or after check-in. Pre-book the Premium or Retreat package well in advance. January daylight is very limited (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:00), so embrace the evening darkness as part of the Icelandic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort. Afterward, join a guided Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour departing from the capital (approx. 45-minute private transfer from resort). Explore Viking heritage, visit Hallgrímskirkja Church, and sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including skyr, hákarl, and freshly baked rye bread.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Reykjavik cultural tour through the harbor district. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall, browse the boutiques on Laugavegur Street, and explore the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Norse and Icelandic history. Private guide available throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour: Depart from Reykjavik in a small luxury group into the Icelandic wilderness far from city light pollution. Expert guide uses real-time aurora forecasts to find optimal viewing locations. Wrapped in warm blankets with hot cocoa provided.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet Icelandic breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — skyr parfaits, smoked lamb, fresh-baked breads, and hot spring eggs
meals.lunch: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant offering a seasonal New Nordic tasting menu
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur — historic Icelandic recipes reimagined in a stylish setting; try the salt cod head and lamb soup

day_by_day.notes: January aurora activity is high due to long polar nights. The Northern Lights tour operator will send a weather/aurora alert by afternoon. If clouds obstruct the lights, the tour is typically rescheduled for the following evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Golden Circle tour begins. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the dramatic Almannagjá gorge with your private guide explaining Iceland's geological and parliamentary history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: witness the explosive Geysir geothermal area where Strokkur erupts every 5–10 minutes, then marvel at the thundering Gullfoss waterfall. All stops are experienced with your private guide and luxury 4WD vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Optional second attempt at Northern Lights viewing from the resort's private beachfront terrace if aurora forecast is favorable. Resort staff will alert you if lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch prepared by the resort's chef, served in a heated luxury vehicle at Þingvellir — smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, Icelandic flatbreads
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Restaurant near Geysir — dine inside a geothermal greenhouse surrounded by tomato plants; famous for their tomato soup and fresh pasta

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is one of Iceland's most iconic routes. In January, roads may be icy — your private driver will have a 4WD vehicle with winter tires. Dress in thermal layers; windproof outer shell essential at Gullfoss.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at the resort. Enjoy the resort's private hot spring facilities or indoor heated pool. Optional yoga or spa treatment session. Relax and recharge before an adventure-heavy day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull: Private transfer (approx. 2 hours) to the Sólheimajökull glacier on the South Coast. Strap on crampons and explore Iceland's stunning glacial landscape with a certified guide. Trek across blue ice formations, peer into crevasses, and learn about climate change's impact on the glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the iconic Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss waterfalls en route back — both dramatically lit in winter darkness. Return to resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Hot soup and artisan sandwiches packed by the resort's kitchen, enjoyed at the glacier base camp with a thermos of Icelandic coffee
meals.dinner: Slippurinn Restaurant (Westman Islands-inspired cuisine) or Rauða Húsið (The Red House) in Eyrarbakki — locally sourced langoustine and Arctic char in a cozy premium setting

day_by_day.notes: Sólheimajökull glacier hike is suitable for all fitness levels with a private guide. Crampons and ice axes are provided. Wear waterproof boots and thermal layers. The glacier is approximately 2 hours from the resort — private luxury transfer recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak: Private transfer to Flúðir village (approx. 1.5 hours). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating back to 1891, surrounded by geysers and steam vents. Far more intimate than the Blue Lagoon — a truly authentic Icelandic bathing experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and its surrounding geothermal landscape. Visit a local mushroom farm that uses geothermal energy for cultivation. Return leisurely to the resort with a scenic drive through the Icelandic countryside.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour (second scheduled attempt): Head out with expert aurora guides into optimal darkness zones. If the previous tour on Day 2 was successful, this evening can alternatively be spent at the resort's spa or attending a private stargazing session arranged by the concierge.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Greenhouse dining at Friðheimar (if not visited Day 3) or a gourmet packed lunch from the resort enjoyed at Secret Lagoon
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — request the chef's tasting menu featuring Icelandic lamb, langoustine bisque, and skyr-based desserts paired with Icelandic craft beer and wine

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offers a more rustic, authentic experience. Swimwear required; towels and robes available for rent or bring your own. January temperatures can be -5°C to -10°C — the contrast of cold air and warm water (38–40°C) is exhilarating.

day_by_day.morning: Private Snæfellsnes Peninsula day trip begins (approx. 2-hour drive north). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth.' Explore dramatic lava fields, sea cliffs, and black sand beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Snæfellsnes Peninsula: visit Arnarstapi's dramatic coastal cliffs and natural rock arch, the charming fishing village of Stykkishólmur, and the Búðakirkja black church for iconic photography. Explore Vatnshellir lava tube cave with a guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Relaxing evening with a private hot tub session on the beachfront terrace. If aurora forecast is strong, the resort's beachfront location offers an excellent natural viewing platform.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Narfeyrarstofa Restaurant in Stykkishólmur — renowned for fresh seafood chowder and locally caught fish in a warm, historic setting
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining experience at Aegean Bliss Resort — curated menu by the executive chef delivered to your beachfront suite with candle service

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is often called 'Iceland in Miniature' due to its diverse landscapes. Roads can be challenging in January — private 4WD transfer essential. The peninsula is one of Iceland's best spots for Northern Lights viewing due to its distance from Reykjavik's light pollution.

day_by_day.morning: Full spa and wellness morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Book a signature Icelandic volcanic stone massage, geothermal facial, or hydrotherapy session. Enjoy the resort's private hot spring pools and steam rooms at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Reykjanes Peninsula — the volcanic peninsula the resort sits on. Visit the Bridge Between Continents (walk between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its dramatic mud pools, and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at the resort's beachfront bar (sunset approx. 16:30). Followed by a premium Northern Lights viewing session — the Reykjanes Peninsula's coastal darkness makes it an excellent aurora viewing spot. Resort staff will alert guests if the lights appear.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — including fresh-baked pastries, smoked fish platters, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the resort's wellness café — superfood bowls, Icelandic lamb broth, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Suður-Vik Restaurant near Grindavík — intimate premium dining featuring local seafood and Icelandic craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally a slower-paced recovery day after six days of active exploration. The Reykjanes Peninsula is the resort's immediate surroundings — all activities are within 30 minutes. This is also a good day to purchase Icelandic souvenirs from premium local artisan shops in Grindavík.

day_by_day.morning: Private fly-over tour of Iceland's volcanic interior via helicopter (approx. 2–3 hours): Soar over Þórsmörk valley, active volcanic fissures, and the Eyjafjallajökull volcano. Land on a remote glacier for a Champagne toast with panoramic views. This is a once-in-a-lifetime premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort. Afternoon at leisure — explore the resort's private beach, enjoy the library lounge with Icelandic literature, or arrange a private photography session with the resort's in-house photographer to capture your Iceland memories.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Guided Tour (third opportunity): Expert guides take the group to a pre-scouted optimal location based on the evening's aurora forecast. Hot drinks and warm blankets provided. Photography assistance available for capturing the lights.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Champagne and canapés on the glacier during the helicopter tour — arranged by the tour operator
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavik (private transfer arranged) — rooftop fine dining with panoramic city views; Icelandic lamb rack and Atlantic lobster tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter tour must be booked at least 3 months in advance and is weather-dependent. The operator will confirm the morning of the flight. If cancelled due to weather, a private super-jeep tour into the volcanic highlands is an excellent alternative. Cost is premium — approximately €800–1,200 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Private South Coast full-day tour begins. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — walk behind the cascading falls (weather permitting in January). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for dramatic photography in the winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara — one of the world's most beautiful beaches with dramatic basalt column formations and Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Continue to the charming town of Vík for a warm break. Optional visit to Dyrhólaey promontory for sweeping coastal views.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey with a stop at a local horse farm for a private Icelandic horse encounter — these unique, gentle horses are a beloved national symbol. Return to resort for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Strondin Bistro & Bar in Vík — hearty Icelandic lamb soup and fresh-baked bread in a cozy setting with views of the black sand beach
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — fresh catch of the day, pan-seared Arctic char with herb butter, and a curated Icelandic wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and stay well back from the waterline. Your private guide will brief you on safety. The South Coast is approximately 1.5–2 hours from the resort; the full loop is a long but spectacular day.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the geothermal wonders of the Haukadalur Valley — beyond the standard Golden Circle. Visit lesser-known hot springs, fumaroles, and geothermal pools with a geology expert guide. Learn about Iceland's position on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and its extraordinary volcanic energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kerið volcanic crater lake — a stunning red caldera with a vivid turquoise lake. Walk the crater rim and descend to the lake shore. Afterward, explore the Skálholt Cathedral, Iceland's historic religious center, with a private cultural guide.
day_by_day.evening: Aurora photography masterclass at the resort: Join a professional astrophotographer for a private session on capturing the Northern Lights with your camera or smartphone. Then head to the resort's beachfront for a live aurora viewing session (forecast dependent).

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch from the resort — smoked lamb wraps, Icelandic cheeses, and hot mushroom soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant), Reykjavik — sushi and Asian-Icelandic fusion using the freshest local seafood; premium sake and cocktail pairing available

day_by_day.notes: The aurora photography masterclass can be arranged through the resort concierge or a local professional photographer. Equipment (tripods, camera settings guidance) is provided. This is an excellent activity for photography enthusiasts wanting to bring home stunning aurora images.

day_by_day.morning: Whale watching private charter from Reykjavik harbor (approx. 45-minute transfer): Board a premium small-group vessel for a 3-hour whale watching tour in Faxaflói Bay. In January, look for humpback whales, minke whales, and harbor porpoises. Heated cabin and hot drinks onboard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for premium shopping on Laugavegur Street. Visit Farmers & Friends for Icelandic design goods, Kirsuberjatré cooperative for local artisan crafts, and 66°North for premium Icelandic outdoor wear. Private styling session can be arranged at select boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at Skál! craft bar in Reykjavik — Iceland's premier cocktail bar featuring Nordic-inspired drinks. Followed by the evening's grand dinner reservation.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) at Reykjavik harbor — legendary lobster soup and grilled fish skewers; a beloved Reykjavik institution
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's most exclusive dining experience; a 20-seat chef's counter with a 20-course tasting menu by chef Ragnar Eiríksson; advance reservation essential (book months ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January has excellent success rates. The premium private charter ensures a more intimate experience than larger tourist boats. Dress in the warmest possible layers — the open sea is significantly colder than land. The Óx reservation is extremely difficult to secure; book immediately upon confirming your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final Blue Lagoon visit — book the exclusive Retreat Spa package for the ultimate send-off. Enjoy private changing suites, the Retreat lagoon (adults-only, tranquil section), a full body ritual treatment, and a gourmet lunch at the Retreat Restaurant. This is the most premium Blue Lagoon experience available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for final packing and a relaxing afternoon. Enjoy a farewell hot spring soak in the resort's private pools. Request a late checkout if available. Browse the resort's gift shop for premium Icelandic souvenirs — lava salt, birch wood products, and local skincare.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset and Northern Lights farewell watch from the resort's beachfront terrace with a glass of Champagne. Final dinner at the resort's finest table with a curated tasting menu celebrating 12 days of Icelandic adventure.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: The Retreat Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — elevated New Nordic cuisine with lagoon views; langoustine tartare and Icelandic lamb loin
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort — private farewell dinner on the beachfront terrace (weather permitting) or in the resort's finest private dining room; full tasting menu with Icelandic wine and spirits pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Retreat Spa at Blue Lagoon is the most exclusive tier of the Blue Lagoon experience and should be booked months in advance. Prices are significantly higher than the standard experience but include exceptional amenities. This is the perfect way to bookend the trip, having visited on Day 1 and Day 12.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Pack remaining items and complete checkout. Take a final morning walk along the beachfront to soak in the Icelandic atmosphere — look for the steam rising from geothermal vents along the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport (20–30 minutes from resort). Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium lounge access. Browse the duty-free shops for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín schnapps, Flóki Whisky), Nói Síríus chocolates, and Icelandic beauty products (Skyn Iceland skincare).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, glacier hikes, and world-class cuisine. Safe travels.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy every last bite of Icelandic skyr, smoked salmon, and freshly baked rúgbrauð (geothermal rye bread)
meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport premium lounge or Isavia Airport Restaurant — fresh Icelandic fish of the day
meals.dinner: Onboard flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport is only 20–30 minutes from the resort — one of the most convenient airport-to-hotel distances in Iceland. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. The airport duty-free offers excellent Icelandic products at competitive prices — stock up on Brennivín, Icelandic wool products, and local skincare. Confirm private transfer the evening before.
